picks.title: Agent Reach
picks.summary: Open-source CLI and SKILL.md kit that gives AI agents read/search access to 15+ internet platforms (Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, Xiaohongshu, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, RSS) with an ordered primary+backup backend per platform and an 'agent-reach doctor' health check.
picks.implementation_idea: An indie developer building a market-research agent could use the kit so the agent itself pulls fresh public sentiment from Reddit, X, and YouTube transcripts, producing a daily competitor briefing without paying for multiple social APIs.
picks.reason: Strongest build idea in the feed

picks.title: VoiceStudio: open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative with voice cloning, dubbing and dictation in 646 languages
picks.summary: VoiceStudio is an open-source, fully-local voice AI studio: voice cloning from a 3-second sample, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobook creation in 646 languages. Ships via Docker with an official Google Colab notebook for zero-install use.
picks.implementation_idea: A media or education startup can run privacy-safe voice cloning and multilingual video dubbing on its own servers, generating localized audiobooks or course narration in dozens of languages with no per-minute API cost.
picks.reason: Strongest build idea in the feed

picks.title: AIHOT — open-source framework for building automated industry-news sites
picks.summary: Full-stack framework (Node 24 + PostgreSQL) that ingests RSS/webpages/X/WeChat, dedupes, double-scores, clusters with embeddings into hot topics, and publishes daily/weekly/monthly reports; 4,000+ GitHub stars within ~42 hours of release.
picks.implementation_idea: A media startup or indie hacker could fork it into a vertical news station (legal, finance, climate) by swapping the source list and taxonomy; a research team could use its SelectBench evaluators to benchmark their own news-selection pipelines.
picks.reason: Strongest build idea in the feed

picks.title: Modular open-sources MAX inference server, Mojo stdlib and accelerator kernels
picks.summary: The core of Modular's unified AI deployment stack is now open: the MAX inference server (OpenAI-compatible endpoints), the Mojo standard library, and the MAX accelerator kernels, all in the modular/modular repo.
picks.implementation_idea: A team paying per token for summarization can stand up MAX as an OpenAI-compatible local server and switch models or hardware without changing application code.
